public_rationale: NIST reports a result supporting the narrower claim that fixed guardrails cannot provide universal robustness. The underlying paper supplies a formal policy-checking framework. That is substantial support, but extending it to every possible useful LLM guardrail requires assumptions absent from Marcus's statement. Neither observed jailbreaks nor the absence of a verified counterexample closes that gap.
limitations: A narrower reading restricted to fixed conventional guardrails would receive stronger support.
The NIST summary was updated after the post, though before the evaluation cutoff.
No independent formal verification of the paper was performed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: For LLMs, it is not possible to guarantee that guardrails cannot be circumvented by jailbreaks.

statement.excerpt: At least with respect to LLMs, the security experts are right.
statement.document_title: Breaking: Trump asks the impossible of Anthropic

our_interpretation: The contextual claim concerns a guarantee against every jailbreak for a useful general-purpose LLM.
Passing a finite test does not establish such a guarantee. Finding failures in existing systems does not by itself establish impossibility.
I assess the technical position during June 1–17, 2026. This is a present technical assertion, not a forecast.
The qualification about LLMs defines the scope; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: A technical impossibility result establishes that useful general-purpose LLM guardrails cannot provide the claimed guarantee, with assumptions matching the claimed scope.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A useful general-purpose LLM system has a verified guarantee against all jailbreaks under the same scope and threat model.

evidence.explanation: The manuscript formalizes policy checking for prompt-based attacks and separately treats unlimited and finite context windows. Applying that formalization to every possible useful guardrail requires a scope assumption Marcus did not state; this version also predates the target period.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A validated impossibility result covering the stated class of useful LLM systems, or a verified jailbreak-proof counterexample under a clearly matched threat model.
